ai.title: Add LITE agent mode to CLI
ai.summary: Introduces LITE mode to the CLI agent system, mapping to the base2-lite agent. Updates constants, slash commands, mode toggle UI, and settings validation to include the new mode. The base2-lite prompt enforces spawning editor-gpt-5 without passing prompts or params.

eli5.text: The CLI now has a fourth agent mode you can switch to: LITE, joining the existing DEFAULT, MAX, and PLAN options. It shows up as a new button labeled LITE in the mode toggle and as a new 'mode:lite' slash command you can type, and switching the mode cycles through DEFAULT -> LITE -> MAX -> PLAN in that order. Under the hood, LITE mode runs a lighter-weight agent that, once it decides it needs to make changes, will hand off to the editor assistant and let that assistant decide what to do on its own rather than being told what to write. It's live today for anyone using these agent modes.

ai.title: agent-mode-toggle test updated for PLAN mode
ai.summary: Updated `agent-mode-toggle.test.ts` assertion to expect 5 segments (4 modes + 1 indicator) instead of 4. Reflects addition of PLAN mode to agent mode toggle. Internal test fix.

eli5.text: When you switch between work modes in the assistant, it now shows one more choice than before. The list of modes you can cycle through grew from three options plus an active indicator to four options plus an active indicator, because a fourth mode was added. This is a behind-the-scenes test that confirms the mode switcher displays the right count; it doesn't add a new feature you can see, but it keeps the software checking itself so the switcher won't break as the modes expand.

ai.title: CLI release 1.0.536 ships LITE agent mode, OSC theme pre-detection
ai.summary: CLI 1.0.536 ships the LITE agent mode tied to the base2-lite agent, which enforces spawning editor-gpt-5 without passing prompts or params, alongside case-insensitive current-mode markers in the slash menu via use-suggestion-engine. The updater now extracts binaries into a temporary directory and smoke-tests them with --version before replacing the active executable, preventing corrupt installs from disrupting updates. OSC theme detection now runs synchronously before TUI startup, and OpenRouter error messages include truncated provider metadata for upstream debugging.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field updated from 1.0.535 to 1.0.536, reflecting a release-bump commit containing only the one-line version change with no modified source beyond the release manifest.

eli5.text: This release adds a new LITE agent mode for lighter, faster AI assistance, plus major improvements to how your terminal theme and slash command menus work. The CLI now automatically detects your terminal's color scheme before launching (so you always see the right theme without flickering), it clearly shows which agent mode you're currently using right in the slash command menu, and the update process is now safer with built-in verification that prevents broken or incompatible versions from replacing your working app. You also get clearer error messages when AI providers fail, more reliable paste handling from your clipboard, and generally smoother, more stable terminal sessions overall.

ai.title: Consolidate agent mode definitions into single source of truth
ai.summary: Refactored CLI to derive agent modes, labels, commands, and cycling logic from a new `AGENT_MODE_TO_ID` constant in `cli/src/utils/constants.ts`. This replaces hardcoded arrays and switch statements in `agent-mode-toggle.tsx`, `slash-commands.ts`, `use-send-message.ts`, `chat-store.ts`, and `settings.ts`. The change ensures all surfaces stay synchronized when modes are added or removed.

eli5.text: All the code that defines what each assistant mode does (like DEFAULT, LITE, MAX, PLAN), what label it shows in the menu, what command you type to switch to it, and what happens when you tap the mode-toggle button to cycle through them has been merged into one single, shared list. Before this, every part of the app that mentioned modes kept its own separate copy, so they were duplicated and prone to getting out of sync if a mode was added or renamed. Now there's just one canonical source that everything reads from. You won't see any new mode or behavior on your screen. This is pure behind-the-scenes housekeeping to make the code safer and easier to maintain.

eli5.text: When you type a multi-line message in the terminal assistant, you can now click anywhere in your text to move the cursor there, instead of nudging it character by character with arrow keys. If you highlight some text with your mouse and then press Delete, only that highlighted part disappears rather than everything from the cursor to the end of the line. The assistant also figures out the real width of your terminal window on its own, so text wrapping behaves correctly even when tabs or wide characters are involved.

ai.title: CLI supports pasting image file paths
ai.summary: CLI paste handler now detects image file paths in clipboard text or drag-drop events, prioritizing them over raw image data. Implemented via `getImageFilePathFromText` in `cli/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts` and wired through `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts` and `cli/src/utils/strings.ts`. This ensures dragged files or copied paths attach correctly instead of relying on potentially stale clipboard image buffers.

eli5.text: When you paste or drag something into the command-line tool, it now checks if the pasted content is an image file path first, before falling back to raw image data. This means dragging a photo directly into the chat or pasting a copied path will attach the actual file correctly, instead of relying on potentially stale clipboard image buffers. The assistant now prioritizes these file paths, which fixes cases where dragging files or copying paths would previously fail to attach properly.

ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release package `codebuff` is bumped to 1.0.538 in `cli/release/package.json`, continuing the same-day release sequence from 1.0.537. This release ships two user-visible CLI improvements: the multiline input now supports mouse clicks to position the cursor and selection-aware deletion via a new `renderPositionToOriginal` helper that maps tab-expanded render positions to original text coordinates, deprecating the `width` prop in favor of dynamic viewport measurement; and the paste handler now detects image file paths from clipboard text or drag-drop events, prioritizing them over raw image data through `getImageFilePathFromText` in `cli/src/utils/clipboard-image.ts`, wired through `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts` and `cli/src/utils/strings.ts`.
ai.evidence: Commit `1449d03e` modifies `cli/release/package.json`, changing the version field from 1.0.537 to 1.0.538. The same-day release instructions list two user-visible features shipped since 1.0.537: click-to-position cursor and selection-aware deletion in the multiline input, and support for pasting image file paths detected from clipboard text or drag-drop events.

eli5.text: This release makes chatting with Freebuff in your terminal smoother and more reliable. You can now click directly inside the text box to place your cursor where you want to type (or move it after a selection), so editing long, multi-line prompts feels like a regular text editor instead of guessing where the caret lands. The CLI also got smarter about pasted content: if you copy or drag an image file path, it recognizes that and attaches the image, instead of depending on whatever stale picture data might sit in your clipboard. Upgrading gives you a faster, less error-prone way to build and edit prompts, with cursor placement and image handling that work the way you'd expect from everyday apps.

ai.title: Fix multiline input navigation and history bugs
ai.summary: MultilineInput now calculates visual line boundaries from TextBufferView.lineInfo for Home/End keys, replacing stale logical line calculations. The getOrSetStickyColumn helper updates its dependency array to include cursorPosition, ensuring accurate sticky column tracking during vertical navigation. Line deletion via Ctrl+Shift+K (or similar) now sets lastEditDueToNav to false, preventing unintended history state pollution.

eli5.text: When you're typing a long message that wraps across several lines on your screen, pressing the up or down arrow now correctly remembers which column you were in on each line, even if the words wrap. Home and End also move you to the actual start and end of what's shown on screen rather than just the start or end of the text itself. Deleting an entire wrapped line with Ctrl+Shift+K no longer accidentally corrupts your undo history, so stepping back won't drop you into an unexpected earlier state.

ai.summary: CLI paste handler now detects image files copied from file managers (e.g., Finder) via new readClipboardImageFilePath utility. Supports macOS AppleScript furl extraction and Windows PowerShell GetFileDropList with -STA flag. eli5.text: If you copy an image file from Finder (macOS) or File Explorer (Windows) and then paste it, the assistant will now correctly recognize it as the file it is, rather than falling back to potentially outdated image data that was already in your clipboard. The system now checks the clipboard for a file path first, and only reads the raw image data if no file path is found. This means pasted images are more reliable and match the file you actually copied. This change is live today.

This release bundles two earlier fixes: Home/End key navigation now computes visual line boundaries from `TextBufferView.lineInfo` instead of stale logical line calculations in `multiline-input.tsx`, and the paste handler prioritizes image file paths copied from file managers (e.g., macOS Finder, Windows Explorer) via the new `readClipboardImageFilePath` utility wired through `use-chat-keyboard.ts` and `strings.ts`. No additional code changes are included in this commit itself. The version bump serves as the release packaging step for these already-merged CLI improvements.

eli5.text: This CLI update improves how you navigate and edit text in the app, and it makes pasting images into your workspace much easier. First, scrolling up and down through long, multi-line messages now moves the cursor exactly where you expect it to, fixing frustrating jumps that happened when pressing Home, End, or arrow keys. Second, you can now copy an image file from your computer's file manager (like macOS Finder or Windows Explorer) and paste it directly into the CLI using the normal paste shortcut, which automatically reads the image without needing extra steps. These changes make writing and editing conversations feel smoother and reduce the guesswork when working with images.

Standard `send-keys` drops characters due to OpenTUI keyboard handling; wrapping input in `\e[200~...\e[201~` ensures atomic processing. eli5.text: When the assistant tries to type answers inside a terminal window that's being driven by an automation tool, the letters get cut off and only the last character shows up. To fix this, the assistant now wraps every message in special invisible markers that tell the terminal the text is arriving all at once, so every letter gets through correctly. If you watched someone script the assistant inside that terminal background, they would have seen words arrive incomplete before, and they would see them arrive whole now.

ai.title: Fix context pruner tool-call/result pair integrity
ai.summary: Context pruner now preserves tool-call and tool-result pairs during message-level pruning to satisfy Anthropic API compliance. Pass 3 logic changed to build a map of paired indices, ensuring these messages are never removed individually. This prevents API errors caused by orphaned tool results or calls. The fix applies to `.agents/context-pruner.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant's conversation memory gets trimmed down to save space, it now keeps tool-call and tool-result pairs together instead of deleting them individually, preventing errors that occurred when only one part of a paired interaction was removed. This affects how the system manages long conversations internally, and if you were watching the trimming process happen, you'd notice that related back-and-forth actions are no longer at risk of being split apart.

ai.title: Context pruner fixes token counting and orphaned tool calls
ai.summary: Context pruner replaces rough JSON length estimation with media-aware token counting, assigning fixed 1000 tokens per image. New logic validates tool-call/tool-result pairs, removing orphaned messages before and after pruning. This prevents context overflow errors and invalid message sequences. Changes are internal to .agents/context-pruner.ts.

eli5.text: When you have a long conversation with an AI assistant, the system sometimes trims older parts to stay within limits, but it had two problems: it guessed how much room messages took by their text length, and it sometimes left behind mismatched tool calls and results. Now it counts messages more accurately, giving each image a fixed 1000-token cost, and it quietly removes any tool call or result that lacks a matching partner before and after trimming. You would notice that the assistant no longer trips over context overflow errors or broken back-and-forth tool sequences during long sessions, since both fixes are internal and already active in the current CLI version.
